text:
maria: Quick check — I'm about to merge a TF change that adds a new GPU nodepool (a2-highgpu-1g) with a zonal capacity reservation in us-west-2c. Need :eyes: on spot fallback behavior and secrets/KMS wiring. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infra/pulls/412

alex: What's the capacity reservation preference? regional vs zonal matters for AZ fallback.

maria: Zonal, we created an explicit Capacity Reservation in us-west-2c and referenced it in the nodegroup. We also set `spot = true` on a mixed-instance nodepool that should be used as fallback. Terraform snippet for CR block: 
```hcl
resource "aws_instance" "gpu" {
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.gpu_cr.id
    }
  }
}
```

jon: Two quick notes: (1) If CR is zonal, add node affinity / topology spread so pods that need reserved GPUs land in that AZ. (2) For spot fallback, prefer separate nodegroups (reserved vs mixed) and control scheduling with taints/labels — easier than trying to coerce a single group.

priya: Also double-check the KMS key used for encrypting kubelet/SSM secrets is allowed for the node IAM role. We hit kms:Decrypt denied last time.

kevin: For scheduling: add label `gpu.capacity=resv` on the reserved nodes and taint `reserved=true:NoSchedule`. Pods that must hit the reserved pool get `nodeSelector` or `tolerations`. For spot fallback, autoscaler should scale the mixed pool; consider a small buffer (min=1) so rolling updates don't spike latency.

maria: Good. I was planning to add: 
- taint on reserved pool 
- nodeSelector in the gpu daemonset template (runtime pods) 
- an eviction hook for spot instances that triggers GRACE drain and moves low-priority pods to mixed pool.

priya: For the IAM change, add the KMS policy to the node role like: 
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
}
```
Make sure the key policy also trusts the account/nodes.

infra-bot: deploy-check: lint OK, tf-plan produced expected changes, integration-tests queued.

deploy-bot: scheduled rollout to staging at 03:00 UTC (will create canary 1/5 first).

alex: small nit: in the TF module, make `capacity_reservation_id` optional (default = null) and `preferred_az` a variable so we can reuse the module in other regions. If `capacity_reservation_id` is null, skip the CR block.

maria: Will update the PR with the optional var + taint/label changes and add the KMS policy to the node role. Planning to merge after a quick staging smoke run. Anyone object?

jon: +1 from me — please record the staging run results in the PR.

kevin: +1. Also add a short runbook entry describing how to fail over to dedicated pools if the capacity reservation is reclaimed or loses capacity.

maria: Will add the runbook and ping on-call after merge. Thanks all :rocket:
